business_problem: Shenli Technology wanted its AI companion products to feel faster, more consistent, and more emotionally believable as user volume grew. Earlier setups struggled with response latency in high-frequency interaction, limited handling of long-form or emotionally complex tasks, weak character consistency over long conversations, and high content-production cost for keeping products fresh.
solution_summary: Shenli Technology redesigned its AI companion stack around a layered Qwen architecture delivered through Alibaba Cloud Bailian. Instead of sending every request to one model, the company routes routine high-frequency interactions to Qwen3-flash for low latency and concurrency, while longer story generation, emotional counseling, or more difficult reasoning tasks are escalated to Qwen3-plus and Qwen3-max. Those model outputs are then passed through Shenli's product-specific prompt engineering, memory strategy, and action-driving logic so the same base model family can power two different companion products: AI Xiyangyang for children and AI Kitty Walulu for young adults. The model layer is embedded across input understanding, scenario recognition, response orchestration, memory accumulation, action tags for the physical toy, and automated content generation, creating a closed loop that balances latency, cost, character consistency, and creative freshness.

solution_components.name: Bailian
solution_components.role: Hosts the model-serving and orchestration environment for Shenli's AI companion products.

solution_components.name: Qwen3-flash
solution_components.role: Handles high-frequency everyday interactions that need fast response and strong concurrency.

solution_components.name: Qwen3-plus
solution_components.role: Supports more complex dialog and story-generation workloads when lightweight inference is not enough.

solution_components.name: Qwen3-max
solution_components.role: Provides the deepest reasoning for emotionally and narratively complex companion scenarios.

data_flow: User voice or text inputs are routed into Bailian, where Shenli's scene-recognition logic decides whether the request should be handled by Qwen3-flash, Qwen3-plus, or Qwen3-max. The resulting outputs are then transformed by role prompts, memory policies, and action tags before they are returned to the physical or app-based companion experience.
business_outcome: Shenli raised the quality and commercial competitiveness of its companion hardware by turning the model stack into a layered production system. Response speed improved 15%, complex task completion improved 15%, repurchase improved 5%, and daily usage time improved 10%, while automated script generation also reduced content-production cost and shortened feature-iteration cycles.
architecture_clues: Different Qwen variants are selected dynamically by scenario instead of using one model for all interactions.
The same base models support multiple consumer products through differentiated prompts, memory policies, and action logic.
Model outputs include both language and action tags, allowing the physical companion device to react in character.
Automated content generation is treated as part of the runtime architecture, not only a back-office content tool.
